label: A1
stem: Use the cipher wheel. The outer ring has the message letters and the inner ring has the code letters (shift 3). What does the message letter D become?
solution: Find D on the outer ring; the inner ring next to it shows G.

label: A2
stem: Using the same wheel, Arun wrote the code word ELUG. What was his message?
solution: Go from inner to outer ring: E→B, L→I, U→R, G→D.

label: A3
stem: With a shift of 1, the name of a number becomes UFO. Which number is it?
solution: Move each letter 1 place back: U→T, F→E, O→N gives TEN.

label: A4
stem: With a shift of 1, how will the word SIX be written?
solution: S→T, I→J, X→Y.

label: A5
stem: The letter X is coded with some shift and becomes C. What is the shift?
solution: X→Y→Z→A→B→C is 5 moves.

label: A6
stem: Mohan coded DOG as FQI. Rina coded CAT using the SAME shift. What did Rina write?
solution: D→F is a shift of 2; CAT becomes ECV.

label: A7
stem: In a Caesar cipher, the same letter always gets the same code letter. Which word can NEVER be the code for BOOK, whatever the shift?
solution: BOOK has two O's together, so its code must have two same letters together. EQRN does not.

label: A8
stem: A shift of 25 places is the same as moving every letter …
solution: 26 places brings a letter back to itself, so 25 forward is 1 short: the same as 1 back.

stem: Each letter tile can be used only once. Which TWO number names can be made at the same time using these tiles?
solution: SIX uses S, I, X and TEN uses T, E, N: all six tiles, once each.

stem: Number names are hidden in this grid. Read ACROSS (left to right) and DOWN (top to bottom). How many number names can you find?
solution: Across: ONE, TWO. Down: TEN (column 1), SIX (column 4).

stem: The bar graph shows how many letters there are in the names of four numbers A, B, C and D. The four numbers are 2, 3, 4 and 6 in some order, and A is smaller than D. Which number is D?
solution: TWO 3, THREE 5, FOUR 4, SIX 3 letters. B = 3, C = 4; A and D are 2 and 6, and A < D, so D = 6.

stem: In a secret code, each letter is shown by a shape. The code for ONE is shown below. What number does the code stand for?
Using the same code, how will you write TEN?
Write the number of dots on each card in words. Which card's name has DIFFERENT number of letters from the others?
solution: FOUR, FIVE and NINE have 4 letters; THREE has 5.

stem: The names of the numbers 1 to 10 are written in dictionary order. Which number's name comes FIRST?
solution: EIGHT starts with E, which comes before F, N, O, S and T.

stem: Which number name has the MOST vowels?
solution: ELEVEN 3, TWELVE 2, FIFTEEN 3, SEVENTEEN 4 vowels.

stem: How many consonants are there in the name EIGHTEEN?
solution: G, H, T, N are consonants: 4.

stem: Take away all the RED coaches from this train. Which number name do the letters on the other coaches spell, from left to right?
solution: Without T and O, the coaches read F I V E.

stem: What comes next? TWO, FOUR, EIGHT, ?
solution: Each number is double the one before: 2, 4, 8, 16.

stem: Read the letters on the snake from its head to its tail. How many number names can you find if the letters must be next to each other? (A letter can be part of two names.)
solution: THREE, EIGHT and TWO (EIGHT shares the E of THREE and the T of TWO).

stem: Kabir writes the names of the numbers 1 to 10. How many times does he write the letter E?
solution: ONE 1, THREE 2, FIVE 1, SEVEN 2, EIGHT 1, NINE 1, TEN 1 = 9.

stem: Which letter appears in the MOST number names from ONE to TEN?
solution: E is in 7 names; N and T are in 4 each; O is in 3.

stem: Add the number of letters in the names of 2, 3 and 4. What do you get?
solution: TWO 3 + THREE 5 + FOUR 4 = 12.

stem: Which number from 1 to 10 has EXACTLY as many letters in its name as its own value?
solution: FOUR has 4 letters.

stem: Read the clue cards. Which number am I?
solution: ELEVEN has 6 letters and ends with N. TWELVE ends with E.

stem: Read the clue cards. Which number am I?
solution: SIX has 3, EIGHT 5 and TWO 3 letters; FOUR has 4.

stem: Each letter can be used only once. Which number name can be made ONLY by using letters from all three kinds of shapes (circles, triangles and squares)?
solution: SEVEN needs S, V, E (circles), the second E (square) and N (triangle). SIX, TEN and ONE can be made from two kinds of shapes.

stem: Cross out the letters of SIX from this strip. Which number do the remaining letters spell, in order?
solution: Left: T, E, N.

stem: Cross out the letters of ONE from this strip. Which number do the remaining letters spell, in order?
solution: Cross out O, N, E: T, W, O are left.

stem: Which number name, when read BACKWARDS, makes another English word?
solution: TEN backwards is NET.

stem: In which number name are ALL the letters different?
solution: SEVEN has two E's, THREE two E's, NINE two N's.

stem: The first letters of the names of 1 to 5 are O, T, T, F, F. What are the first letters of the names of 6 to 10?
solution: SIX, SEVEN, EIGHT, NINE, TEN.

stem: Each letter has a value equal to its place in the alphabet (A = 1, B = 2 … Z = 26). Which number name has the SMALLEST total?
solution: ONE 34, TEN 39, SIX 52, TWO 58.

stem: Which ONE letter fills ALL the blanks? N _ N E · F _ V E · S _ X · E _ G H T
solution: NINE, FIVE, SIX, EIGHT all need I.

label: P1
stem:
Tina, Sam and Esha each picked a different card: 3, 7 or 8.
- Nobody's card name starts with the same letter as their own name.
- Tina's card is not 7.
Who picked card 3?
solution: Tina can't have THREE (T) or 7, so she has 8. Sam can't have SEVEN (S), so he has 3. Esha has 7.

label: P2
stem:
Ravi, Meena, Joy and Kiran each read a story on a different day from Monday
- Ravi reads on the day whose name has the MOST letters.
- Meena reads on the day just before Ravi.
- Joy does not read on Monday.
Who reads on Thursday?
solution: WEDNESDAY has 9 letters, so Ravi is Wednesday and Meena Tuesday. Joy is not Monday, so Joy is Thursday.

stem: Tara made this robot using solid shapes. How many CYLINDERS has she used?
solution: 2 arms and 2 legs are cylinders.

stem: Look at Tara's robot again. Which solid has she NOT used?
solution: It has a cube head, cone hat, cuboid body and cylinders, but no sphere.

stem: Which of these objects has NO flat face?
solution: A ball is round all over. The dice, cone and tin all have flat faces.

stem: How many cubes are there in this staircase?
A big cube was made of small cubes, 2 cubes long, 2 wide and 2 tall. One small cube has been taken away. How many small cubes are left?
Four cubes are placed like this. What will they look like from the TOP?
solution: From the top you see 3 squares in an L. The top cube sits on a bottom cube, so it adds no new square.

stem: Look at the cubes from the direction of the arrow. What will you see?
solution: Three columns side by side: 1 cube, 3 cubes, 1 cube.

stem: This tent is shaped like a triangular prism. How many faces does it have?
solution: 2 triangles (front and back) + 3 rectangles = 5.

stem: How many corners does this square pyramid have?
solution: 4 corners on the square base + 1 at the top = 5.

stem: How many edges does the tent (triangular prism) in Question 8 have?
solution: 3 edges on the front triangle, 3 on the back and 3 joining them = 9.

stem: Solids are sorted into this diagram. In which part should a CYLINDER go?
solution: A cylinder has flat faces AND a curved surface, so it goes in the overlap Q.

stem: In the same diagram, in which part should a CUBE go?
solution: A cube has only flat faces, so it goes in P.

stem: Which object can be stacked one on top of another AND can also roll?
solution: Tin cans stack on their flat faces and roll on their curved surface.

stem: A torch shines on a party cap (cone) from the SIDE. What shape is its shadow on the wall?
solution: Seen from the side, a cone looks like a triangle.

stem: What is the MOST number of faces of a dice you can see at one time?
solution: From any corner you can see at most 3 faces.

stem: On a dice, the numbers on opposite faces always add up to 7. This dice shows 2 on top. What number is on the BOTTOM face?
Each face of a cube is to be coloured so that no two faces that share an edge have the same colour. What is the LEAST number of colours needed?
solution: Opposite faces don't touch, so give each pair of opposite faces one colour: 3 colours.

stem: Riya made a toy house by placing a square pyramid on top of a cube. The house stands on the floor. How many faces of the house can be seen from all around? (Do not count faces that touch the floor or each other.)
solution: Cube: 4 side faces (top is covered, bottom is on the floor). Pyramid: 4 triangles. 4 + 4 = 8.

stem: Find the odd one out.
solution: Only the cylinder has a curved surface.

stem: Which solid has faces that are ALL the same shape and the same size?
solution: All 6 faces of a cube are equal squares.

label: P1
stem:
A ball, a cube, a cone and a cylinder stand in a row on a shelf.
- The cube is at the LEFT end.
- The ball is next to the cone.
- The cylinder is not next to the cube.
Which toy is at the RIGHT end?
solution: Cube is 1st. The cylinder can't be 2nd, and the ball and cone must be side by side, so they take 2nd and 3rd and the cylinder is 4th.

label: P2
stem:
Ravi, Mini and Joy each built a tower and put a different solid on top: a cone, cube.
- Ravi's top solid has no flat face.
- Mini's top solid has a pointed tip.
Whose tower has the cube on top?
solution: No flat face means a sphere (Ravi). A pointed tip means a cone (Mini). The cube is Joy's.

stem: The abacus shows a number. If 2 beads are moved from the Ones rod to the Tens rod, what number will it show?
solution: It shows 147. After the move: 1 hundred, 6 tens, 5 ones = 165.

stem: What number do these blocks show? (A big square = 100, a long rod = 10, a small cube = 1)
solution: 100 + 30 + 12 = 142. The 12 small cubes make 1 ten and 2 ones.

stem: An abacus has three rods: Hundreds, Tens and Ones. You must use EXACTLY 4 beads and put at least one bead on every rod. What is the LARGEST number you can show?
solution: Put 1 bead on each rod first; the extra bead goes on Hundreds: 211.

stem: A frog starts at 100 and keeps jumping 30 steps forward each time. Its first two jumps are shown. Which number will it NOT land on?
solution: It lands on 130, 160, 190 … so it never lands on 170.

stem: This is a part of a number chart. Which number is hidden under the star?
solution: Third row is 161–165; the 4th box is 164.

stem: On the same chart, start at 143. Move one box DOWN and then one box to the RIGHT. Where are you now?
solution: Down from 143 is 153; right of 153 is 154.

stem: Raju has this money. How much more does he need to buy a cricket bat that costs ₹ 200?
Tina counts in fifties: 50, 100, 150 … How many numbers does she say until she reaches 200? (Count 200 too.)
Using each card exactly once, how many 3-digit numbers between 100 and 200 can be made?
solution: Only 108 and 180 start with 1.

stem: Using the same three cards once each, which 3-digit number is CLOSEST to 150?
solution: 180 is 30 away; 108 is 42 away; 801 and 810 are far.

stem: Each bundle has 10 sticks. How many sticks are there in all?
solution: 12 bundles = 120 sticks; 120 + 6 = 126.

stem: The house numbers follow a pattern. What is the number on the green house?
solution: Each number is 11 more than the one before: 133 + 11 = 144.

stem: Read the clue cards. Which number am I?
solution: Ones = 5, tens = 7, hundreds = 1: 175.

stem: The scoreboard shows the scores in a game. Who scored the SECOND highest?
solution: 198 (Bina) is highest; 191 (Dev) is next.

stem: Rohan writes all the numbers from 100 to 110. How many times does he write the digit 1?
Find the odd one out.
solution: The first three are 150; 1 hundred 50 tens is 600.

stem: Which number reads the SAME from the left and from the right?
solution: 181 backwards is still 181.

stem: Move from START to END, going only RIGHT or DOWN. Add the numbers on every box you pass (START and END too). What is the BIGGEST total you can get?
solution: Down, Right, Down, Right: 50 + 30 + 60 + 40 + 50 = 230.

stem: In the same grid, which path gives a total of EXACTLY 200?

options: 4th and Solve every clue carefully. Make

label: P1
stem:
Asha, Bina and Chetan each pick one card: 125, 152 or 215.
- Asha's number is the largest.
- Bina's number has 5 in the tens place.
Who picked 125?
solution: Asha has 215, Bina has 152, so Chetan has 125.

label: P2
stem:
My 3-digit locker code is between 100 and 200.
- Its digits add up to 10.
- Its ones digit is double its tens digit.
What is the code?
solution: Hundreds = 1. Tens + ones = 9 and ones = 2 × tens, so tens = 3, ones = 6: 136.

stem: Riya travels from Home to Nani's Village. What is the length of the SHORTEST route?
solution: Home → A → B → Village = 25 + 10 + 30 = 65 km.

stem: On the same map, how much LONGER is the route Home → B → Village than the shortest route?
Nani Maa, Mummy, Riya and Tinu (both children) take the bus. How much do they pay in all?
Nani wants all three baskets to have the SAME number of mangoes. How many mangoes will each basket have?
The pictograph shows the bananas eaten during the holiday. How many MORE bananas were eaten on Tuesday than on Wednesday?
solution: Tuesday 5 × 2 = 10, Wednesday 2 × 2 = 4; 10 − 4 = 6.

stem: How many bananas were eaten in all four days?
Papa drives and Mummy sits next to him. Nani sits just behind Papa. Riya sits next to Nani. Tinu also sits at the back. Who sits just behind Mummy?
solution: Back row: behind Papa is Nani, then Riya in the middle, so Tinu is behind Mummy.

stem: A number goes into the machine and 60 comes out. What number went in?
solution: Work backwards: 60 + 10 = 70; 70 − 25 = 45.

stem: Look at Nani Maa's family tree. How many grandchildren does Nani Maa have?
solution: Riya, Tinu, Arjun, Pari and Gul = 5.

stem: Cousins are the children of your parent's brothers and sisters. How many cousins does Riya have in this tree?
solution: Arjun, Pari and Gul. Tinu is her brother, not a cousin.

stem: A train has 12 coaches. Riya's coach is 5th from the engine and Nani's coach is 3rd from the end. How many coaches are BETWEEN them?
solution: 3rd from the end = 10th from the engine. Coaches 6, 7, 8, 9 are between.

stem: Kites are tied in a row in this repeating pattern. What colour is the 15th kite?
solution: The pattern red, blue, blue, yellow repeats every 4. 15 = 12 + 3, so it is the 3rd colour: blue.

stem: Riya collected 34 shells and Tinu collected 18. How many shells should Riya give Tinu so that both have the same?
solution: Total 52, so 26 each; Riya gives 34 − 26 = 8.

stem: Riya has ₹ 50. She buys EXACTLY 3 items and spends ALL her money. Which could she have bought?
solution: 20 + 20 + 10 = ₹50. The others make ₹40, ₹45 and ₹35.

stem: Riya rolls a dice three times and gets 4, 6 and 2. Tinu gets 5 and 5 in his first two rolls. What is the SMALLEST number he needs on his third roll to get a bigger total than Riya?
solution: Riya's total is 12. Tinu has 10 and needs more than 12, so at least 3.

stem: A bucket is pulled up from a well 12 m deep. Each pull lifts it 4 m, but it slips back 1 m before the next pull. After how many pulls does it reach the top?
solution: After pulls 1, 2, 3 it is at 3, 6, 9 m (after slipping). Pull 4 lifts it to 13 m.

stem: Find the odd one out.
solution: All are 60 except 80 − 30 = 50.

stem: Nani has three mango trees. Tree B has 30 mangoes. Tree A has 10 more than B. Tree C has 5 fewer than B. How many mangoes in all?
A bus starts with 40 people. At stop 1, 12 get off and 20 get on. At stop 2, 15 get off and 7 get on. How many people are on the bus now?
Nani's village is 85 km from the city. The bus has already gone 38 km. How much farther must it go?

label: P1
stem:

- Riya is older than Tinu.
- Mona is not the oldest.
- Tinu is not the youngest.
Who is 9 years old?
solution: Tinu is not youngest, and Riya is older than him, so Tinu is 9 and Riya is 10. Mona is 7.

label: P2
stem:

- Hen C laid as many as A and B together.
- Hen D laid 3 eggs.
How many eggs did Hen B lay?
How many of these shapes have EXACTLY 4 corners?
solution: Square, rectangle, rhombus and trapezium.

stem: How many triangles are there in this figure?
solution: 3 triangles in the top part (left, right, both together) and 3 using the whole height: 6.

stem: How many squares are there in this figure?
solution: 6 small squares and 2 bigger squares made of 4 small ones.

stem: These two triangles are the same size. Which shape can you make by joining them along one side, without overlapping?
solution: Joining the long sides makes a square.

stem: How many sides does this shape on the dot paper have?
solution: Count the straight edges around the L-shape: 6.

stem: Which picture shows this flag after a HALF turn?
solution: A half turn turns it upside down.

stem: In which picture will the two parts match EXACTLY when the paper is folded along the red line?
solution: Only the line through the middle of the rectangle splits it into matching halves.

stem: Three squares in a row are made with 10 matchsticks. How many matchsticks are needed for 5 squares in a row?
solution: Start with 4 sticks; each new square adds 3: 4 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 16.

stem: How many rectangles (count squares too) can you see in this house?
solution: The wall, the door and the window.

stem: I have 4 equal sides, but my corners are NOT square corners. Who am I?
solution: A rhombus has 4 equal sides with slanted corners.

stem: Each row and each column has one circle, one square and one triangle. Which shape goes in place of "?"
solution: Row 3 and column 3 are both missing a square.

stem: What comes next?
solution: Each shape has one more side: 3, 4, 5, then 6.

stem: Find the odd one out.
solution: In the others, the number tells the number of sides. The pentagon has 5 sides, not 6.

stem: A square and a circle overlap. Into how many parts do they divide the space INSIDE them?
solution: Square only, circle only, and the part in both.

stem: Two squares of the same size are joined so that one full side touches. How many corners does the new shape have?
solution: Together they make a rectangle, which has 4 corners.

stem: A round pizza is cut with 2 straight cuts, both going through the centre. How many pieces are there?
solution: Two cuts through the centre make 4 pieces.

stem: Another pizza is cut with 3 straight cuts, all going through the centre. How many pieces are there?
solution: Each cut through the centre adds 2 pieces: 6.

stem: How many triangles are used to make this rocket?
solution: The nose and the two fins.

stem: In a 4 × 4 grid, Riya colours every box in the top row and every box in the left column. How many boxes are coloured?
solution: 4 + 4 = 8, but the top-left box is counted twice: 7.

stem: Ravi draws 3 triangles and 2 squares. How many sides do all his shapes have together?

stem:

- The triangle is between the circle and the square.
- The star is at the right end.
- The circle is not at the left end.
Which shape is at the LEFT end?
solution: Star is 4th. The triangle is between the circle and the square, so it is 2nd. The circle is not 1st, so the square is.

label: P2
stem:

- R's shape has no corners.
- S's shape has 6 corners.
- P's shape has more corners than Q's.
Which shape does P have?
solution: R has the circle and S the hexagon. P has more corners than Q, so P has the square.

stem: Move 2 beads from the Hundreds rod to the Ones rod. By how much does the number become SMALLER?
Using 3 different cards, what is the LARGEST 3-digit EVEN number you can make?
solution: Put 9 first, then 4, and end with the even digit 2: 942. (984 uses an 8, which is not a card.)

stem: Using the same cards, what is the SMALLEST 3-digit ODD number you can make?
solution: It must end in 9 and cannot start with 0: 209.

stem: Read the clue cards. Which number am I?
solution: Only 528 and 538 are between 520 and 540; 5 + 3 + 8 = 16.

stem: A number lock shows 472. Each dial can only turn UP by 1 at a time. Riya turns the Hundreds dial up 2 times and the Ones dial up 3 times. What number does it show now?
solution: Hundreds 4 → 6, Ones 2 → 5: 675.

stem: Which number is the same as 6 hundreds and 4 ones?
Find the odd one out.
solution: The others are all 700; 7 tens is 70.

stem: The doors on a street are numbered 405, 415, 425 and so on. What is the number on the 6th door?
The house numbers follow a pattern. What is the number on the green house?
solution: Each number is 100 less: 712 − 100 = 612.

stem: How many of these numbers are LESS than 200?
solution: Only 132 and 123 start with 1.

stem: How many 3-digit numbers have 5 in the hundreds place AND 0 in the ones place?
Read the clue cards. Which number am I?
solution: Hundreds 1, tens 2, ones 1 + 2 = 3: 123.

stem: A number on an abacus uses 12 beads in all. The Hundreds rod has 5 beads and the Ones rod has none. What is the number?
solution: Tens rod has 12 − 5 = 7 beads: 570.

stem: Which marked number is CLOSEST to 350?
solution: A = 318, B = 362, C = 389, D = 341. D is only 9 away from 350.

stem: Swap the tens and ones digits of 482. What is the difference between the old number and the new number?

Which number is 10 more than 395?
A 3-digit number has all DIFFERENT digits, and its digits add up to 6. What is the LARGEST such number?
solution: 600 repeats 0. The next largest is 510 (5 + 1 + 0 = 6).

stem: How many whole numbers are there BETWEEN 250 and 260?
solution: 251 to 259 = 9 numbers.

label: P1
stem:
Four players wear shirts numbered 105, 150, 501, 510.
- Tom has the largest number.
- Sam's number is less than 200 and even.
- Raj's number is odd.
- Vik's number is smaller than Raj's.
What is Raj's number?
solution: Tom 510, Sam 150. Raj and Vik share 105 and 501; Vik is smaller, so Raj has 501.

label: P2
stem: In this number pyramid, each block is the sum of the two blocks just below number goes at the top?
solution: Middle row: 350 and 375. Top: 350 + 375 = 725.

stem: Meena has these rakhis. She gives one full row to each of her 3 brothers. How many rakhis are left?
solution: 4 rows of 6 = 24; she gives 3 rows = 18; 24 − 18 = 6.

stem: Each sweet box has 3 rows of 4 laddoos. How many laddoos are there in 2 such boxes?
A grasshopper starts at 0 and keeps jumping 4 steps forward. Which number will it land on?
In this table, each box has (row number × column number). Which number is hidden under the star?
solution: Row 4, column 3: 4 × 3 = 12.

stem: In the same table, how many boxes have the number 12?
Each rakhi needs 15 cm of thread. Meena has a 70 cm long thread. How many rakhis can she make, and how much thread is left?
Riya puts 40 laddoos into packs of 6. How many FULL packs does she make, and how many are left over?
27 chocolates are to be shared equally among 4 brothers. At least how many MORE chocolates are needed so that none are left over?
solution: 28 is the next number in the table of 4; 28 − 27 = 1.

stem: Look at the two puzzles. What number is the circle?
solution: Star = 5 (5 + 5 + 5 = 15). 5 × circle = 20, so circle = 4.

stem: In a family, each of the 3 sisters ties a rakhi on each of the 4 brothers. How many rakhis are tied in all?
solution: Each sister ties 4 rakhis: 3 × 4 = 12.

stem: Laddoos are kept in 4 equal rows of 5. A cloth covers some of them. How many laddoos are UNDER the cloth?
solution: 4 × 5 = 20 in all; 8 can be seen; 20 − 8 = 12.

stem: Find the odd one out.
solution: The others are 24; 5 × 4 = 20.

stem: Riya has 3 rakhis. Mona has 4 times as many. How many rakhis do they have together?
Pick TWO cards and multiply their numbers. What is the BIGGEST answer you can get?
solution: 4 × 5 = 20 is the largest.

stem: Chairs are arranged in rows of 7. There are 5 full rows and 3 extra chairs. How many chairs are there?
A flower plant has 2 flowers on Day 1, and the number of flowers doubles every day. How many flowers will it have on Day 5?
A number multiplied by itself gives 36. What is that number plus 10?
Which number is in the table of 3 AND in the table of 4?
solution: 24 = 3 × 8 = 4 × 6. The others are in only one table.

stem: Gift boxes are stacked like this, with no gaps inside. How many boxes are there?
solution: Each layer has 2 rows of 3 = 6 boxes; 3 layers = 18.

stem: Bangles are sold in sets of 4 for ₹ 20 a set. Mona buys 12 bangles. How much does she pay?
solution: 12 bangles = 3 sets; 3 × ₹20 = ₹60.

stem:

- Bina ties the blue rakhi.
Who ties the red rakhi?
solution: Bina has blue and Asha is not red, so Chinu has red.

stem:

- Box A has double the sweets in Box B.
- Box C has fewer sweets than Box A.
How many sweets are in Box C?
solution: D = 15. A = 2 × B gives A = 12, B = 6. C gets 8, which is fewer than 12 ✔

stem: In which picture is the shaded part NOT a half of the shape?
solution: The square has only 1 of its 4 parts shaded: a quarter.

stem: Riya eats half of this chocolate. Then Tinu eats half of what is left. How many pieces remain?
solution: 8 pieces → Riya eats 4 → 4 left → Tinu eats 2 → 2 left.

stem: Two slices of this pizza have been eaten. What part of the pizza is LEFT?
solution: 6 of 8 slices are left. 6 slices = 3 groups of 2, and 2 slices = a quarter, so three quarters are left.

stem: A paper is folded along the red line and a half-circle is cut out from the fold. What will the paper look like when it is opened?
solution: The half-circle on the fold opens into a full circle in the middle.

stem: ₹ 40 is shared equally among 4 children. One child then gives half of his share to his sister. How much does he have now?
solution: Each gets ₹10; half of ₹10 is ₹5.

stem: What part of this grid is shaded?
solution: 8 of the 16 boxes are shaded: half.

stem: Which letter can be folded along a straight line into two matching halves?
solution: A can be folded down its middle; F, G and J cannot.

stem: The two bottles (half a litre and a quarter litre) are poured into the empty 1 litre jug. How much MORE water is needed to fill the jug?
solution: Half + a quarter = three quarters; one more quarter fills the jug.

stem: Start with 64. Take half of it, then half again, then half again. What number do you get?

solution: One cut gives either two triangles or a triangle and a four-sided piece. A pentagon has 5 corners, which is not possible.

solution: The 4 side triangles go round the pyramid, so 2 colours can alternate on them. The base touches all 4 triangles, so it needs a third colour.

solution: 6 cubes have 6 × 6 = 36 faces. You can see 12 of them (front, top and right sides), so 36 − 12 = 24 cannot be seen.

stem: Six cubes are stacked as shown. How many faces of these cubes can NOT be seen in the picture? Note: Count every face of every cube, even the ones touching another cube.
solution: 6 cubes have 6 × 6 = 36 faces. You can see 11 of them (front, top and right sides), so 36 − 11 = 25 cannot be seen.

stem: A square pyramid has some corners marked with a yellow dot or a red dot. How many edges have a yellow dot at one corner but do NOT have a red dot at the other corner?
solution: Go edge by edge: count the edges that touch a yellow corner and whose other end is yellow or blank (not red). Total: 5.

- The star is not in Box 4.
Which shape is in Box 3?
solution: Triangle is in Box 1. The star can be in Box 2 or 3. If it is in Box 2, the circle and square take boxes 3 and 4, which are neighbours. So the star is in Box 3.

stem:
All four shapes of the Set go into the four squares, one in each, so that:
- A shape is never put in a square of its own colour.
- Two squares joined by a line must hold different kinds of shape (a circle and a
- triangle).
- Square 1 holds a triangle.
Which shape goes in Square 4?
solution: Square 1 holds a triangle, so Squares 2 and 4 hold circles and Square 3 a triangle. Square 3 is green, so it takes the yellow triangle, and the green triangle goes in Square 1. Square 2 is blue, so it takes the red circle, leaving the blue circle for Square 4.

stem: Ria walks from Start to End and visits every block. She picks up one flower from every block except the block that comes immediately after a GREY block. How many flowers does she pick?
solution: There are 10 blocks. The blocks right after the grey ones (blocks 4, 7 and 10) give no flower, so 10 − 3 = 7.

stem: Tara walks from Start to End and visits every block. She picks up a shell only from the block that comes immediately after a GREY block. How many shells does she pick?
solution: The blocks right after the grey blocks 2, 5 and 7 are blocks 3, 6 and 8. She picks 3 shells.

stem: A bee flies from S to E, always following the arrows. How many different paths can it take?
solution: Paths: S-A-C-E, S-A-D-E and S-B-D-E. So there are 3 paths.

stem: An ant walks from S to E, always following the arrows. How many different paths can it take?
solution: Through D: S-A-D, S-B-D give 2 paths to E. Through F: S-B-F, S-C-F give 2 paths. 2 + 2 = 4.

stem: Three children A, B and C walk along the coloured paths, each starting from the dot. Who takes the fewest turns?
solution: Count the corners of each path: A has 1, B has 3, C has 2. So A turns the least.

stem: Kavi starts at the dot and walks along the red path in the direction of the arrow. How many times does he turn to his right?
solution: Going up, he turns right at the top-left corner (1). Going right then he turns right to go down (2), then left to go right again. So he turns right 2 times.

stem: Sam wants to reach Home by walking only on the grey strip. Which piece fills the gap in the strip? Note: You are not allowed to rotate the option pieces.
solution: The gap starts right after the vertical part and goes down 2 squares, then turns right for 2 squares. Only this shape fits.

stem: Mia climbs along the grey strip, going upwards and to the right. Which piece fills the gap in the strip? Note: You are not allowed to rotate the option pieces.
solution: The gap goes up 1 square and then right 2 squares more. This is the only piece with that shape in that position.

stem: An arrow points at the square right next to it in the direction it shows. Which letter has the most arrows pointing at it?
solution: Count the arrows pointing straight at each letter: A: 2, B: 2, C: 3, D: 1.

stem: An arrow points at the square right next to it in the direction it shows. Which letter has the fewest arrows pointing at it?
solution: Count the arrows pointing straight at each letter: P: 2, Q: 3, R: 1, S: 0.

stem: Which picture shows the top view of the towers of cubes? Note: You cannot rotate the question image or the options.
solution: Looking from the top, each column or row of cubes shows as squares in the picture. This matches the correct option.

stem: Which picture shows the top view of these cubes? Note: You cannot rotate the question image or the options.
solution: Looking from the top, each column or row of cubes shows as squares in the picture. This matches the correct option.

stem: Tia has built this tower from coloured cubes. Which view shows the most different colours? Note: Count only the colours you can see from that side.
options: All views show the same number
solution: Front view shows 3 colours, right-side view 3 and top view 4. So Top view shows the most.

stem: Tia has built this tower from coloured cubes. Which view shows the most different colours? Note: Count only the colours you can see from that side.
options: All views show the same number
solution: Front view shows 2 colours, right-side view 2 and top view 3. So Top view shows the most.

stem: Which tower looks like picture X when you look at it from the front? Note: You cannot rotate the picture or the options.
solution: Look at the towers from the front: the tallest stack in each column or row must match the picture X.

stem: Which tower looks like picture X when you look at it from the right side? Note: You cannot rotate the picture or the options.
solution: Look at the towers from the right side: the tallest stack in each column or row must match the picture X.

stem: A boy stands on Block 3 (the pink block) and faces the animals. Where is the Fox with respect to the Cat, from his point of view?
solution: He faces the left side of the page. The Fox is on the right of the Cat on the page, which is behind the Cat for a boy looking to the left.

stem: A girl stands on Block 1 (the pink block) and faces the animals. Where is the Hen with respect to the Goat, from her point of view?
solution: She faces the right side of the page. The Hen is above the Goat on the page, which is on her left when she looks to the right.

solution: Looking from the top, each column or row of cubes shows as squares in the picture. This matches the correct option.

stem: Ten stickers are shared among four children A, B, C and D. One child gets 1 sticker, another 2, another 3 and another 4. B gets more than A, and D gets fewer than C. If C gets at least two more stickers than D, which statement is always true?
options: B gets at least 2 more stickers than A
A and D together get 4 stickers
B and C together get 7 stickers
C gets more stickers than B
solution: C and D can be (3, 1), (4, 1) or (4, 2). Trying each with B > A gives only (A,B,C,D) = (1,3,4,2), (2,3,4,1), (2,4,3,1). In all of them B + C = 7.

stem:
Five children A, B, C, D and E stand in a line, from left to right.
- A, D and E are not at either end of the line.
- B stands immediately to the right of A.
- C is at one of the ends, but D is not next to C.
Who stands in the middle?
solution: A, D and E are not at the ends, so the ends are B and C. B is right of A, so B is on the right end, C on the left. D is not next to C, so the line is C, E, D, A, B. D is in the middle.

label: A1
stem: A white coin in Row 2, Column 4 of a grid is flipped to black. Before the flip every row and column had an even number of black coins. What changes in that row and that column?
solution: Even + 1 = odd. A black coin is added to that row and to that column, so both now have an odd number of black coins.

label: A2
stem: A black coin in a grid is flipped to white. How many rows and how many columns now have an odd number of black coins?
solution: The flipped coin lies in exactly one row and one column. Each of them loses one black coin, so just that row and that column become odd.

label: A3
stem: The 5 × 5 grid had an even number of black coins in every row and column. Then one coin was flipped. Which coin was it?
solution: Only Row 2 and Column 1 have an odd number of black coins, so the coin where they cross was flipped.

label: A4
stem: The 5 × 5 grid had an even number of black coins in every row and column. Then one coin was flipped. Which coin was it?
solution: Only Row 3 and Column 1 have an odd number of black coins, so the coin where they cross was flipped.

label: A5
stem: Here is a 3 × 3 pattern. Which 4 × 4 pattern is made by adding one extra row and one extra column so that every row and every column has an even number of black coins?
solution: Count the black coins in each row and write 0 or 1 at its end to make the count even. Do the same for each column. The correct option is the one where every row and column count is even.

label: A6

solution: Count the black coins in each row and write 0 or 1 at its end to make the count even. Do the same for each column. The correct option is the one where every row and column count is even.

stem: A grid starts as a 5 × 5 pattern. One extra row and one extra column are added. How many coins are needed for the extra row and column?
solution: The new row has 6 coins (5 + the corner) and the new column has 5 more: 6 + 5 = 11.

label: A8
stem: A grid starts as a 7 × 7 pattern. One extra row and one extra column are added. How many coins are needed for the extra row and column?
solution: The new row has 8 coins (7 + the corner) and the new column has 7 more: 8 + 7 = 15.

stem: Eight squares are to be filled with the numbers 1 to 8, each used once. Four numbers are already filled. If every result is a single-digit ODD number, which of these can NEVER be the result of any of the four sums?
solution: Work out which numbers can go in the blanks so that each result is odd (adding an odd number to an odd gives even, and so on). The results that can appear are [1, 5, 7, 9]; 3 never appears.

stem: Eight squares are to be filled with the numbers 1 to 8, each used once. Four numbers are already filled. If every result is a single-digit ODD number, which of these can NEVER be the result of any of the four sums?
solution: Work out which numbers can go in the blanks so that each result is odd (adding an odd number to an odd gives even, and so on). The results that can appear are [1, 3, 5, 9]; 7 never appears.

stem: XY is a two-digit even number. The sum of X and Y is a single-digit odd number. At most how many different values can X take?
solution: Y is even, so X must be odd for the sum to be odd. X can be 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9 (for example 10, 32, 54, 76, 90). That is 5 values.

stem: PQ is a two-digit number that is a multiple of 5. The sum of P and Q is a single-digit even number. At most how many different values can P take?
solution: Q is 0 or 5. The numbers are 15, 20, 35, 40, 60 and 80, so P can be 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 or 8. That is 6 values.

stem: Six consecutive odd numbers are written on the faces of a dice. If the smallest number is 7, what is the largest number?
solution: The numbers are 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17. The largest is 17.

stem: Six consecutive even numbers are written on the faces of a dice. If the largest number is 30, what is the smallest number?
solution: Count back by 2 from 30: 30, 28, 26, 24, 22, 20. The smallest is 20.

stem: What comes in place of "?" in the series of dice?
solution: The dots go +2, −1, +2, −1, … After 4 (the −1 step) comes +2, so 4 + 2 = 6.

stem: What comes in place of "?" in the series of dice?
solution: The dots go −2, +1, −2, +1, … After 3 (the +1 step) comes −2, so 3 − 2 = 1.

stem: Every grid on the left changes to the grid on its right by the same rule. What comes in place of "?"
solution: The rule: every number that can be divided by 3 is replaced by a dot (12, 30, 21, 18 and so on). Apply it to the last grid: 6, 3, 18 and 12.

stem: Every grid on the left changes to the grid on its right by the same rule. What comes in place of "?"
solution: The rule: every 2-digit number is replaced by a dot. Apply it to the last grid: 47, 15, 63, 28 and 36 become dots.

stem: Diya wants to pick only the items on the steps marked with even numbers. Which option shows what she collects?
solution: Check each step number: the items on those steps are 2 stars, 2 circles, 0 triangles.

stem: Diya wants to pick only the items on the steps marked with numbers that are multiples of 3. Which option shows what she collects?
solution: Check each step number: the items on those steps are 2 stars, 3 circles, 0 triangles.

stem: Arun tries to put his stickers in pairs, but one sticker is left over every time. How many stickers could he have?
solution: A leftover of 1 after making pairs means the number is odd. Only 31 is odd.

stem: A teacher can make groups of 3 with no child left out, but she cannot make groups 2 without a child left out. How many children could there be?
solution: The number is a multiple of 3 but odd. 24, 30 and 36 are all even; 27 is odd and 3 × 9 = 27.

stem: Statement: The product of two natural numbers is 35. Which of these can be understood from the statement?
options: At least one number is even
The sum of the two numbers is odd
solution: The pairs are 1 × 35 and 5 × 7. In both pairs both numbers are odd, so (b).

stem: Statement: The difference between two natural numbers is 1. Which of these can be understood from the statement?
options: One is odd and the other is even
solution: Numbers that differ by 1 are neighbours on the number line: one is odd and the other is even (like 8 and 9).

stem:
There are only 4 people P, Q, R and S standing in a queue.
- P is not standing at an odd-numbered position from the front
- S is standing immediately behind Q
- R is not standing first
Who is standing last?
solution: Q is immediately ahead of S. P must be at position 2 or 4, R is not first. Only Q, S, R, P works. P is last.

stem:
There are only 4 people A, B, C and D standing in a queue.
- C is not standing at an even-numbered position from the front
- D is standing immediately ahead of A
- A is not standing last
Who is standing last?
solution: Both queues that fit the clues (C, D, A, B and D, A, C, B) have B at the end.

stem:
If any 4 odd numbers in the figure are joined by straight lines in increasing order, which of these figures can NOT be made? Note: The options show only the lines, not the numbers.
- 1 2
- 3
- 4 7 5
8 9 6
solution: Joining odd numbers in increasing order, for example 1-3-5-7 or 3-5-7-9, always gives a path that moves from a smaller number to the next larger one. The chosen figure goes through the numbers in a different order.

stem:
If any 4 odd numbers in the figure are joined by straight lines in increasing order, which of these figures can NOT be made? Note: The options show only the lines, not the numbers. 9 2 8 6
- 3 5
- 1 7 4
solution: Joining odd numbers in increasing order, for example 1-3-5-7 or 3-5-7-9, always gives a path that moves from a smaller number to the next larger one. The chosen figure goes through the numbers in a different order.

stem: Question: Is P × Q an odd number? Statement 1: P is an odd number. Statement 2: Q is an even number. Which statement(s) is/are enough to answer the question?
options: Only 2 The question cannot be answered even if both
solution: An odd × odd is odd, but with only P odd we cannot tell about Q. If Q is even then the product is always even, so Statement 2 alone answers the question (No).

stem: Question: Is A + B an even number? Statement 1: A is an odd number. Statement 2: B is an odd number. Which statement(s) is/are enough to answer the question?
options: Only 2 The question cannot be answered even if both
Both 1 and 2 together The Thinking Spot
solution: One odd number alone does not tell us anything. Together, odd + odd = even, so both statements are needed.

- Yellow is connected only to Red
What is the colour of the circle marked with "?"
solution: Use the clues to place the colours one at a time. Circles with a unique number of lines are easiest to find first. Then the circle marked "?" must be Yellow.

stem: The numbers 64, 29, 91, 37 (from top to bottom) enter the network. What is the order (top to bottom) after Level 1?
solution: Apply the boxes of Level 1; the smaller number of each pair moves up. Order after Level 1: 29, 64, 37, 91.

label: A2
stem: The numbers 72, 18, 45, 53 (from top to bottom) enter the network. What is the order (top to bottom) after Level 2?
solution: Apply the boxes of the levels one by one; the smaller number of each pair moves up. Order after Level 2: 18, 53, 45, 72.

label: A3
stem: In a sorting network every comparison box sends the smaller number up. By mistake a box is built to send the bigger number up instead (in every box). What will the final order be, from top to bottom?
options: The same order as the input
It depends on the input order
From the smallest to the biggest
From the biggest to the smallest
solution: When every box is reversed, the network still sorts, but the other way round: the biggest number reaches the top and the smallest ends at the bottom.

label: A4
stem: Six children stand on the inputs of a sorting network and compare their heights. The shorter child always takes the upper path. What is the order at the output, from top to bottom?
solution: A sorting network always sorts. With the shorter child going up in every box, the shortest ends at the top and the tallest at the bottom.

label: A5
stem: Children compare names in a box. The name that comes first in the dictionary goes to the left. Meera and Maya meet in a box. Who goes left?
solution: Both names start with M. The second letters are A (Maya) and E (Meera). A comes before E, so Maya goes left.

label: A6
stem: A network sorts 8 numbers and 8 numbers are fed in at the start. In the first level every box compares two different numbers and every number goes into one box. How many boxes are in the first level?
solution: Each box takes 2 numbers, and 8 numbers are shared among them: 8 ÷ 2 = 4 boxes.

stem: 4X52 and 45X2 are two 4-digit numbers where X is one digit. Which of these can be true when X is less than 6?
solution: If X is 0 to 4, the hundreds digit decides: 4X52 < 45X2. If X = 5 both numbers are 4552, so they are equal. They can never be greater (X cannot be more than 5).

stem: 27X8 and 2X78 are two 4-digit numbers where X is one digit less than 7. Which of these is always true?
solution: Compare the hundreds digits first: 7 in the first number and X in the second. X is less than 7, so the first number is always bigger.

stem: What is the smallest 4-digit number made from 4 different circles below, such that the number of white circles used is less than the number of black circles used?
solution: There are only 3 black circles (1, 0 and 4), so use all three and one white circle. The smallest number from 1, 0, 4 and the smallest white digit 3 is 1034.

stem: What is the largest 4-digit number made from 4 different circles below, such that the number of white circles used is more than the number of black circles used?
solution: At least 3 of the 4 circles must be white, so use 5, 4, 2 (all the white ones) and one black circle. The largest arrangement puts the largest digits first: 9542.

stem: In the expression 58X3 > 5X83, X stands for one digit. How many different values from Set B can X take so that the statement is true?
solution: Test each value of X: the true ones are [1, 3, 4, 6, 7].

stem: In the expression 2X91 < 29X1, X stands for one digit. How many different values from Set B can X take so that the statement is true?
solution: Test each value of X: the true ones are [3, 6, 8].

stem: Using the digits 9, 2, 5, 7, 0, 4 and 6, make the largest and the smallest 4-digit numbers so that no digit repeats within a number. Which digit is common to both numbers?
solution: Largest: 9765. Smallest: 2045 (0 cannot be first). The only digit in both is 5.

stem: Using the digits 8, 3, 6, 1, 9, 4 and 2, make the largest and the smallest 4-digit numbers so that no digit repeats within a number. Which digit is common to both numbers?
solution: Largest: 9864. Smallest: 1234. The only digit in both is 4.

stem:

- 61097 56957 78304 71198
- Number 1 Number 2 Number 3 Number 4
solution: The common digit is 7. Taking it out leaves 6109, 5695, 8304, 1198. The largest is 8304, from Number 3.

stem:

- 45623 14238 60747 67943
- Number 1 Number 2 Number 3 Number 4
solution: The common digit is 4. Taking it out leaves 5623, 1238, 6077, 6793. The largest is 6793, from Number 4.

stem: Which of the following numbers can come in place of "#" in the expression?
solution: # must be more than 3569 and less than 4208. Only 3777 is between them.

stem: Which of the following numbers can come in place of "#" in the expression?
solution: # must be more than 7281 and less than 7829. Only 7365 is between them.

stem: How many numbers from Set A can be placed in the blank to form a number greater than 4562?
solution: Try each digit of Set A: [7, 9] work. That is 2 numbers.

stem: How many numbers from Set A can be placed in the blank to form a number smaller than 7505?
solution: Try each digit of Set A: [2, 4] work. That is 2 numbers.

stem: If you add all the digits in the HUNDREDS place of the numbers shown, what will be the digit in the TENS place of the result?
solution: Hundreds digits: 8, 9, 7. Their sum is 24, so the tens digit is 2.

stem: If you add all the digits in the HUNDREDS place of the numbers shown, what will be the digit in the ONES place of the result?
solution: Hundreds digits: 4, 6, 7. Their sum is 17, so the ones digit is 7.

stem: How many numbers in the box, after swapping their tens and thousands digits, will be less than 5000?
solution: After swapping: 6241, 8375, 4560, 2187. Those below 5000: 2.

stem: How many numbers in the box, after swapping their tens and thousands digits, will be more than 6000?
solution: After swapping: 1925, 3654, 7430, 8092, 2169. Those above 6000: 2.

stem: How many numbers can be placed in both boxes?
solution: Numbers that fit both rules: 3684, 4120, 3830. That is 3.

stem: How many numbers can be placed in both boxes?
solution: Numbers that fit both rules: 6215, 6095, 5960, 6480. That is 4.

solution: Cross out the box of each person and every box joined to it by a line. The boxes left are the meeting boxes: 2.

label: P2
stem: P, Q and R want to meet. They cannot meet in the boxes they are standing in, or in any box that is joined by a line to the box of any of them. In how many boxes can they meet?
solution: Cross out the box of each person and every box joined to it by a line. The boxes left are the meeting boxes: 1.

stem: Each jar below has its capacity split into 8 equal parts. How many jars are filled to less than half their capacity?
solution: Half is 4 out of 8 parts. Jars with 1 or 3 parts filled are less than half: 7 jars.

stem: Each glass below has its capacity split into 8 equal parts. How many glasses are filled to half or more of their capacity?
solution: Half is 4 out of 8 parts. Glasses with 4, 6 or 8 parts are half or more: 7 glasses.

stem: What fraction of the figure is shaded grey? (Some squares are cut into two equal triangles.)
solution: Count in half-squares: 2 whole squares = 4 halves, plus 3 half squares = 7. The figure has 9 squares = 18 halves. So the fraction is 7/18.

stem: What fraction of the figure is shaded grey? (Some squares are cut into two equal triangles.)
solution: Count in half-squares: 3 whole squares = 6 halves, plus 2 half squares = 8. The figure has 8 squares = 16 halves. So the fraction is 8/16.

stem: Rohan bought some notebooks for exactly Rs. 72. Each notebook costs the same. Which of these can NOT be the price of one notebook?
solution: 72 ÷ 6 = 12, 72 ÷ 8 = 9 and 72 ÷ 9 = 8 exactly, but 72 ÷ 10 = 7.2, so a notebook cannot cost Rs. 10.

stem: A baker packs exactly 60 cookies into boxes, with the same number in every box and none left over. Which of these can NOT be the number of cookies in a box?
solution: 60 ÷ 4 = 15, 60 ÷ 5 = 12 and 60 ÷ 12 = 5, but 60 ÷ 8 = 7.5, which is not a whole number.

stem: What will come in place of "?" in the series?
solution: The shaded part grows by 2 eighths each time: 1/8, 3/8, 5/8, so the next is 7/8.

stem: What will come in place of "?" in the series?
solution: The shaded part doubles each time: 1, 2, 4 twelfths, so the next is 8/12.

stem: Which option shows the correct number of minutes in (1/2 + 1/3) hour?
solution: 1/2 hour = 30 min and 1/3 hour = 20 min, so the total is 50 minutes. 60 − 10 = 50.

stem: Which option shows the correct number of minutes in (1/3 + 1/4) hour?
solution: 1/3 hour = 20 min and 1/4 hour = 15 min, so the total is 35 minutes. 7 × 5 = 35.

stem: Find the ODD one out. (The shaded slices are the part that is eaten.)
solution: Three pizzas have 3 of 8 slices shaded. The odd one has 5 of 8 shaded.

stem: Find the ODD one out.
solution: Three bars have half of their parts shaded (3 of 6, 4 of 8, 5 of 10). The odd one has 2 of 5 shaded, which is less than half.

stem: Each pair of bars (the shaded part is the fraction) is followed by a sign that compares the left fraction with the right one. What comes in place of "?"
solution: Compare the shaded parts: left = 3/6, right = 2/4. So the sign is =.

stem: Each pair of bars (the shaded part is the fraction) is followed by a sign that compares the left fraction with the right one. What comes in place of "?"
solution: Compare the shaded parts: left = 3/5, right = 3/4. So the sign is <.

stem: Each shape is changed into a fraction by the same rule. What comes in place of "?"
solution: The number of red sides is the top number and the total number of sides is the bottom number.

stem: Each shape is changed into a fraction by the same rule. What comes in place of "?"
solution: The number of red sides is the top number and the total number of sides is the bottom number.

stem: A piece of paper is shaped like a rectangle that is not a square. At most how many times can it be folded so that each fold divides it into two identical halves?
solution: A rectangle that is not a square can be folded in half along its length or along its width. The diagonals do not give identical halves by folding. So 2 folds.

stem: A piece of paper is a triangle with exactly two equal sides. At most how many times can it be folded so that each fold divides it into two identical halves?
solution: Only the line from the corner between the two equal sides to the middle of the opposite side makes two identical halves. So 1 fold.

stem: In each row the shape on the left changes into a pie on the right by the same rule. What comes in place of "?"
solution: The number of shaded parts (out of 8) is the number of sides of the shape. A hexagon has 6 sides, so 6 of 8 parts are shaded.

stem: In each row the pie on the left changes into a shape on the right by the same rule. What comes in place of "?"
solution: The shape has 2 more sides than the number of shaded parts (out of 6). 4 shaded parts give a shape with 6 sides.

label: P1
stem: Six children are in a group. Each child shares sweets with at least one other child, and if A shares with B then B also shares with A. Which of these can never be true?
solution: A child can share with 1 to 5 others, which is only 5 different numbers, but 6 children would need 6 different numbers. (Pairs, a circle of 6, or everyone with everyone all work.)

label: P2
stem: Seven friends meet. Each friend shakes hands with some of the others, and each handshake is between two friends. Which of these can never be true?
solution: Each handshake is counted twice, once for each person, so the total of everyone's handshakes must be even. 7 × 3 = 21 is odd, so it is impossible. (7 × 2 = 14, 7 × 4 = 28 and 7 × 6 = 42 are even.)

stem: Each line runs along a row of 10 equal squares. Some squares are black and hide part of the line. Which line has the longest part hidden behind the black squares?
solution: Count the black squares that sit on each line: the solid line 3, the red dashed line 3, the green dotted line 4. The most is hidden for the green dotted line.

stem: Each line runs along a row of 10 equal squares. Some squares are black and hide part of the line. Which line has the longest part hidden behind the black squares?
solution: Count the black squares that sit on each line: the solid line 3, the red dashed line 3, the green dotted line 4. The most is hidden for the green dotted line.

stem:
If block ___ is removed from the figure, its perimeter will be decreased. Fill in the blank. P T S V
- U Y Q X
- R Z
solution: Removing a block that touches only 1 other block takes away 3 sides and adds 1, so the perimeter goes down by 2. A block touching 2 others leaves it the same, and a block touching 3 others makes it larger.

stem:
If block ___ is removed from the figure, its perimeter will be increased. Fill in the blank.
- A B
C D E F

solution: Removing a block that touches 3 other blocks takes away 1 side and adds 3, so the perimeter goes up by 2. A block touching 2 others leaves it the same, and a block touching only 1 other makes it smaller.

stem: The numbers on the roads show their lengths in km. Asha goes from S (school) to H (home) by the shortest route. How many km does she travel?
solution: Add the road lengths on each route. The shortest route is S-A-B-D-H with 15 km.

stem: The numbers on the roads show their lengths in km. Ravi goes from S (school) to H (home) by the shortest route. How many junctions (circles with a letter, other than S and H) does he pass?
solution: The shortest route is S-A-C-H (13 km). The letters between S and H are the junctions: 2.

stem: Three dogs A, B and C each run along their own coloured path from the dot to the matching bone. Each dog takes exactly the same time (10 minutes). Which dog runs the fastest?
solution: All take the same time, so the dog with the longest path must run the fastest. Path lengths in squares: A = 8, B = 7, C = 9. So Dog C.

stem: Three children P, Q and R walk along their own coloured paths from the dot to the matching circle. Each child takes exactly the same time. Who walks the slowest?
solution: All take the same time, so the child with the shortest path walks the slowest. Path lengths in squares: P = 7, Q = 11, R = 9. So Child P.

stem: If the monkey follows the shortest path from Start to the banana, which option shows 3 tiles that come immediately one after another on its path, in the same order? Note: The monkey moves only up, down, left or right, not diagonally. Start
solution: Trace the shortest route tile by tile: square, square, circle, triangle, circle, diamond …. Only one option appears in this exact order.

stem: If the squirrel follows the shortest path from Start to the nut, which option shows 3 tiles that come immediately one after another on its path, in the same order? Note: The monkey moves only up, down, left or right, not diagonally. Start
solution: Trace the shortest route tile by tile: square, triangle, pentagon, diamond, diamond, square …. Only one option appears in this exact order.

stem: A cuboid is 6 cm long, 3 cm wide and 3 cm high. It is cut into two equal cubes. How many faces of each cube have the same perimeter as an end face (3 cm × 3 cm) of the original cuboid?
solution: Each piece is a cube of side 3 cm, and all 6 of its faces are 3 cm × 3 cm squares with the perimeter 12 cm, same as the end faces.

stem: A rectangular sheet is 8 cm long and 4 cm wide. It is cut into two equal squares. What is the perimeter of one square?
solution: Each square has side 4 cm, so its perimeter is 4 × 4 = 16 cm.

The first to start is the last to finish. Who finishes second?
solution: R-2 or R-3 starts first. Trying both, the only way to follow all rules is: start order R-2, R-3, R-1 and finish order R-3, R-1, R-2. R-1 finishes second.

stem: P and Q have Rs. 150 each. Each of them bought one item. P spent Rs. 80 more than What could be the highest possible amount spent by Q?
solution: P cannot spend more than Rs. 150. P = Q + 80, so Q + 80 ≤ 150 and Q ≤ 70.

stem: X and Y have Rs. 300 each. Each of them bought one item. X spent Rs. 120 more than Y. What could be the highest possible total amount spent by both together?
solution: X can spend at most Rs. 300. Then Y spent 300 − 120 = Rs. 180. Together: 300 + 180 = Rs. 480.

stem: Hari starts with 0 points and climbs the stairs to the top. On each step the points shown are gained (+) or lost (−). Which ONE step must Hari skip to finish with exactly 184 points?
solution: All the steps together give 139 points. To get 184, the skipped step must be worth -45, which is step B.

stem: Gita starts with 0 points and climbs the stairs to the top. On each step the points shown are gained (+) or lost (−). Which ONE step must Gita skip to finish with exactly 193 points?
solution: All the steps together give 163 points. To get 193, the skipped step must be worth -30, which is step A.

stem: Boxes A, B and C each have 400 sweets. Ria took 150 sweets out of box A and 150 sweets out of box B. Then Sam put 50 sweets into each of the three boxes. Which boxes have an equal number of sweets at the end?
options: No two boxes have the same number
solution: Final numbers: A = 300, B = 300, C = 450. So A and B are equal.

stem: Boxes A, B and C each have 600 sweets. Neel took 250 sweets out of box A and 250 sweets out of box C. Mina took 125 sweets out of box B, and then another 125 sweets out of box B. Then Raj put 125 sweets into box A. Which boxes have an equal number of sweets at the end?
options: No two boxes have the same number
solution: Final numbers: A = 475, B = 350, C = 350. So B and C are equal.

stem: A, B and C stand for 3 different single-digit numbers in the rows below. Each option a 3-digit number made from A, B and C. Which option has the highest value?
solution: Solve the rows: A = 3, B = 5, C = 4. The numbers are BAC = 534, BCA = 543, CBA = 453, ACB = 345. The highest is BCA.

stem: A, B and C stand for 3 different single-digit numbers in the rows below. Each option a 3-digit number made from A, B and C. Which option has the highest value?
solution: Solve the rows: A = 7, B = 5, C = 3. The numbers are CAB = 375, ACB = 735, ABC = 753, BAC = 573. The highest is ABC.

stem: What is the LEAST number that can replace "?" so that the sum of Row 2 is greater than the sum of Row 1?
solution: Row 1 adds up to 702. The other two numbers in Row 2 add up to 475. We need ? + 475 > 702, so ? > 227, and the least such number is 228.

stem: What is the LEAST number that can replace "?" so that the sum of Row 2 is greater than the sum of Row 1?

solution: Start 30 white, 25 black. Green: 28, 24. Red: 28, 20. Blue: 23, 20. Red: 23, 16. Green: 21 white, 15 black.

stem: What is the difference between the largest and the smallest 2-digit numbers (with two different digits) that can be made from the digits shown?
solution: Largest = 97, smallest = 24 (a number cannot start with 0). 97 − 24 = 73.

stem: What is the difference between the largest and the smallest 2-digit numbers (with two different digits) that can be made from the digits shown?
solution: Largest = 86, smallest = 30 (a number cannot start with 0). 86 − 30 = 56.

solution: Mark the shape on each side of every triangle (counting a shape each time it is next to a triangle). Counts: Square 3, Circle 1, Pentagon 2. The most is Square.

stem: Shapes are weighing stones of different weights. Look at the balances. Which statement is definitely true?
options: The star is heavier than the square
The square is heavier than the star
The triangle is heavier than the circle
The circle is heavier than the triangle
solution: Triangle is heavier than star, and star is heavier than circle, so triangle is heavier than circle. The square can be heavier or lighter than the star, so the other statements are not sure.

stem: Shapes are weighing stones of different weights. Look at the balances. Which statement is definitely true?
options: The star is heavier than the diamond
The circle is heavier than the star
The diamond is heavier than the circle
The circle is heavier than the diamond
solution: Circle is heavier than square and square is heavier than star, so circle is heavier than star. Whether diamond or circle is heavier cannot be known.

stem: All the balances are level. Each shape has its own weight. How many circles will balance 6 squares?
solution: 2 squares = 3 circles, so 1 square = 1½ circles. 6 squares = 6 × 1½ = 9 circles.

stem: All the balances are level. Each shape has its own weight. How many circles will balance 2 triangles?
solution: 1 triangle = 2 squares and 1 square = 3 circles. So 1 triangle = 6 circles and 2 triangles = 12 circles.

stem: Which word should replace the question mark in circle B, such that every word in circle A has a closely related word in circle B?
solution: Units in A measure the quantities in B: metre → length, gram → mass, minute → time, litre → capacity.

stem: Which word should replace the question mark in circle B, such that every word in circle A has a closely related word in circle B?
solution: Each tool in A measures a quantity in B: ruler → length, clock → time, weighing scale → weight, thermometer → temperature.

stem: A water cooler has 46 litres of water. There are two bags of empty bottles. One bag has 5 bottles of 4 litre capacity each and the other has 7 bottles of 5 litre capacity each. You must empty the cooler by filling at least one bottle from each bag. A picked bottle must be filled completely. What is the MAXIMUM number of bottles that can be left empty?
solution: Use as few bottles as possible: 4 bottle(s) of 4 L and 6 bottle(s) of 5 L give 16 + 30 = 46 L. Bottles used = 10, so empty bottles = 12 − 10 = 2.

stem: A water cooler has 57 litres of water. There are two bags of empty bottles. One bag has 6 bottles of 4 litre capacity each and the other has 8 bottles of 7 litre capacity each. You must empty the cooler by filling at least one bottle from each bag. A picked bottle must be filled completely. What is the MAXIMUM number of bottles that can be left empty?
solution: Use as few bottles as possible: 2 bottle(s) of 4 L and 7 bottle(s) of 7 L give 8 + 49 = 57 L. Bottles used = 9, so empty bottles = 14 − 9 = 5.

stem: You have buckets of capacities 6 litres, 4 litres and 1 litre. You may use a bucket more than once, but each type must be used at least once. What is the minimum number of buckets needed to hold EXACTLY 30 litres of water? (Each bucket must be filled completely.)
solution: Use the big buckets as much as possible while keeping each type at least once: 4 × 6 + 1 × 4 + 2 × 1 = 30. Buckets used = 7.

stem: You have buckets of capacities 7 litres, 3 litres and 1 litre. You may use a bucket more than once, but each type must be used at least once. What is the minimum number of buckets needed to hold EXACTLY 25 litres of water? (Each bucket must be filled completely.)
solution: Use the big buckets as much as possible while keeping each type at least once: 3 × 7 + 1 × 3 + 1 × 1 = 25. Buckets used = 5.

stem: A lift can carry a maximum of 400 kg. Three people with weights 60 kg, 70 kg and 80 kg are already inside. Meera wants to know the maximum extra weight the lift can still carry. How can she find it?
options: Add the three weights and add the result to 400
Add the three weights and subtract the result from 400
Multiply the three weights and subtract from 400
solution: First add the weights of the three people: 60 + 70 + 80 = 210 kg. The extra weight allowed = 400 − 210 = 190 kg.

stem: A tank can hold 500 litres of water. It already has some water in it. Rohan wants to find how many more litres can be poured in without it overflowing. How can he find it?
options: By adding the water in the tank to 500
By multiplying the water in the tank by 500
By subtracting the water in the tank from 500
solution: The space left = capacity − water already in the tank, so subtract the water in the tank from 500.

stem: Anil weighs 9 kg more than Bela. Bela weighs 14 kg less than Chetan. If Chetan weighs 52 kg, find Anil's weight.
Mohan weighs 7 kg more than Sonu. Sonu weighs 20 kg less than Tina. Tina weighs kg more than Uma. If Uma weighs 41 kg, find Mohan's weight.

Q is taller than P and heavier than S. S is taller than R and heavier than T. A heavier person is always taller. Who is the tallest among P, Q, R, S and T?
solution: Q is heavier than S, so Q is also taller than S. S is taller than R and heavier than T, so S is taller than R and T. Q is taller than P, S, R and T. So Q is the tallest.

stem: A is taller than B and heavier than C. C is taller than D and heavier than E. A heavier person is always taller. Who is the shortest among A, B, C, D and E?
solution: Only these facts are known: A is taller than B, C, D and E; C is taller than D and E. We cannot compare B with D or E, nor D with E. Several people could be the shortest.

stem: 24 bottles are arranged from left to right in a single row. The position of a bottle from the left end decides the water in it: the 1st bottle has 1 L, the 2nd has 2 L and so on. If the 5th bottle from the left is interchanged with the 4th bottle from the right, how many litres of water will be in the first 5 bottles from the left?
solution: The 4th bottle from the right is at position 24−4+1 = 21, so it holds 21 L. After swapping, the first 5 bottles hold 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 21 = 31 L.

stem: 30 bottles are arranged from left to right in a single row. The position of a bottle from the left end decides the water in it: the 1st bottle has 1 L, the 2nd has 2 L and so on. If the 2nd bottle from the left is interchanged with the 7th bottle from the right, how many litres of water will be in the first 4 bottles from the left?
solution: The 7th bottle from the right is at position 30−7+1 = 24, so it holds 24 L. After swapping, the first 4 bottles hold 1 + 24 + 3 + 4 = 32 L.

stem: A six-faced dice has the numbers 1 to 6 written on its faces (one number on each face). Which of the following can be definitely implied from the statement? Statement: The number opposite to 5 is greater than it.
solution: The only number greater than 5 is 6, so 6 is opposite to 5. Every other number (1, 2, 3, 4) is then on a face next to 5, so 4 is adjacent to 5.

stem: A six-faced dice has the numbers 1 to 6 written on its faces (one number on each face). Which of the following can be definitely implied from the statement? Statement: The number opposite to 3 is a multiple of 3.
solution: The only other multiple of 3 is 6, so 6 is opposite to 3. All of 1, 2, 4, 5 are then adjacent to 3, so 2 is adjacent to 3.

stem: When 36 is added to a number, the result is four times the number itself. What was the number?
solution: Number + 36 = 4 × number, so 36 equals 3 times the number. Number = 36 ÷ 3 = 12. Check: 12 + 36 = 48 = 4 × 12.

stem: When 50 is added to a number, the result is six times the number itself. What was the number?
solution: Number + 50 = 6 × number, so 50 equals 5 times the number. Number = 50 ÷ 5 = 10. Check: 10 + 50 = 60 = 6 × 10.

stem: On a dice, different numbers from 1 to 6 are written on the faces so that: • 4 is adjacent to ALL the faces having odd numbers • 2 is adjacent to ALL its multiples How many DIFFERENT numbers can possibly be opposite to 1?
solution: Opposite faces are never adjacent. 4 cannot be opposite to 1, 3, 5, and 2 cannot be opposite to 4 or 6. Faces that can be opposite to 1: 2, 3, 5. That is 3 numbers.

stem: On a dice, different numbers from 1 to 6 are written on the faces so that: • 6 is adjacent to ALL the faces having even numbers (other than itself) • 3 is adjacent to ALL its multiples How many DIFFERENT numbers can possibly be opposite to 1?
solution: 6 cannot be opposite to 2 or 4, and 3 cannot be opposite to 6. Faces that can be opposite to 1: 2, 3, 4, 6. That is 4 numbers.

stem: In a row of 60 boys, both Hari and Ishaan are at positions that are multiples of 12 from the left end. Ishaan's position is twice Hari's position, and Hari is not at the 12th place from the left end. What is Ishaan's position from the right end?
solution: Multiples of 12: 12, 24, 36, 48, 60. Hari cannot be at 12, so Hari = 24 and Ishaan = 48. From the right: 60 − 48 + 1 = 13.

stem: In a row of 80 boys, both Tina and Uma are at positions that are multiples of 16 from the left end. Uma's position is twice Tina's position, and Tina is not at the 16th place from the left end. What is Uma's position from the right end?
solution: Multiples of 16: 16, 32, 48, 64, 80. Tina cannot be at 16, so Tina = 32 and Uma = 64. From the right: 80 − 64 + 1 = 17.

stem: A sequence of numbers is given: 7, 21, 63, 189, 567. What is the rule that governs this sequence?
options: Every term is 14 more than the previous term
Every term is twice the previous term
Every term is 7 times the previous term
Every term is three times the previous term
solution: 21 ÷ 7 = 3, 63 ÷ 21 = 3, 189 ÷ 63 = 3, 567 ÷ 189 = 3. Every term is three times the previous term.

stem: A sequence of numbers is given: 4, 9, 19, 39, 79. What is the rule that governs this sequence?
options: Every term is 5 more than the previous term
Every term is twice the previous term
Every term is double the previous term plus 1
Every term is double the previous term minus 1
solution: 4 × 2 + 1 = 9, 9 × 2 + 1 = 19, 19 × 2 + 1 = 39, 39 × 2 + 1 = 79. Each term is double the previous term plus 1.

stem: Mira has some ten-rupee notes. Her friend Tina asks how much money she has. What should Mira do to answer?
options: Multiply the number of notes by 5
Multiply the number of notes by 10
Add 10 to the number of notes
Multiply the number of notes by 100
solution: Each note is worth Rs. 10, so the money is (number of notes) × 10.

stem: Imran has some two-rupee coins and some five-rupee coins. His friend asks how much money he has altogether. What should Imran do?
options: Add the number of two-rupee coins and five-rupee coins and multiply by 7
Multiply the two numbers of coins together
Add the two numbers of coins and multiply by 5
Multiply each number of coins by its coin value and add the two results
solution: Money from two-rupee coins = (number) × 2. Money from five-rupee coins = (number) × 5. Add both amounts to get the total.

stem: A pond is slowly being covered by a plant that doubles in size every day. After exactly 30 days the plant covers the whole pond. After how many days did it cover half of the pond?
solution: The plant doubles every day, so the day before it covers the full pond it covered exactly half. That is day 30 − 1 = 29.

stem: Bacteria in a dish triple every day. After exactly 12 days the dish is full. After how many days was one-third of the dish covered?
solution: Tripling means the amount on the day before is one-third of the amount on the next day. One-third was covered on day 12 − 1 = 11.

stem: I am a vehicle. To carry a group of 50 students, 9 vehicles like me are needed. To carry a group of 40 students, 7 vehicles like me are needed. How many students can I carry at most?
solution: Try capacities: with 6 students per vehicle, 50 students need 9 vehicles and 40 students need 7 vehicles, which matches. A smaller or larger capacity gives a different number of vehicles for at least one group, so the capacity is 6.

stem: I am a vehicle. To carry a group of 70 students, 10 vehicles like me are needed. To carry a group of 45 students, 7 vehicles like me are needed. How many students can carry at most?
solution: Try capacities: with 7 students per vehicle, 70 students need 10 vehicles and 45 students need 7 vehicles, which matches. A smaller or larger capacity gives a different number of vehicles for at least one group, so the capacity is 7.

stem: The number of sisters Amit has is three times the number of brothers he has. Amit has no more than 4 brothers. At most, how many sisters will any sister of Amit have?
solution: If Amit has b brothers, he has 3b sisters. Largest b = 4, so 12 sisters. A sister of Amit has the other 12 − 1 = 11 sisters.

stem: The number of brothers Meena has is three times the number of sisters she has. Meena has no more than 3 sisters. At most, how many brothers will any brother of Meena have?
solution: If Meena has s sisters, she has 3s brothers. Largest s = 3, so 9 brothers. A brother of Meena has the other 9 − 1 = 8 brothers.

stem: If A = 5, Z is three times A, B is double of Z and Y is half of B, Which of the following expressions has the HIGHEST value?
If P = 4, Q is three times P, R is half of Q and S is double of R plus P, Which of the following expressions has the HIGHEST value?
solution: Q = 12, R = 6, S = 16. Values: Q + R + S = 34, 2 × S − Q = 20, S + R + P = 26, 3 × R + P = 22. Highest: Q + R + S.

stem: A square sheet has a side of 12 cm. Which of the following numbers of equal-sized square sheets can NOT be cut from it so that no part of the sheet is left over?
solution: Equal squares fit a square sheet in rows and columns, so their number must be a perfect square (4, 9, 16, 25 ...). 12 is not a perfect square.

stem: A square sheet has a side of 20 cm. Which of the following numbers of equal-sized square sheets can NOT be cut from it so that no part of the sheet is left over?
solution: Equal squares fit a square sheet in rows and columns, so their number is 1×1, 2×2, 3×3 ... = a perfect square. 18 is not a perfect square.

stem: Arrows fly straight in the direction they point, over any cells, until they leave the grid. In how many empty cells can a balloon be placed so that NO arrow can hit it?
solution: Draw the path of every arrow to the edge of the grid and mark each cell it crosses. The empty cells never crossed are safe: (row 1, column 1), (row 1, column 4), (row 4, column 1), (row 5, column 1), (row 5, column 5). That is 5 cells.
